record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: What role does dark matter play in the evolution of the branch-cut universe, including any role it may have in the contraction-era scaling behavior that the authors connect to the epsilon parameter?

evidence.quote: Other aspects to be investigated refer to ... the role of dark matter in the evolution of the branch-cut universe.

This is because, in the final phase of the contraction process, choosing the epsilon parameter with a negative value (dark matter?), the scaling behavior of the ratio is reversed, simultaneously assuming the remaining ratios are locked in.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological model (the "branch-cut universe") whose scale factor is analytically continued across a branch cut, replacing the classical Big Bang singularity with a smooth contraction-to-expansion transition. The dynamics depend on a real parameter epsilon that controls the scaling behavior of characteristic length and density ratios near the bounce. Suppose that in the final phase of the contraction era, taking epsilon < 0 reverses the scaling behavior of one such ratio while the remaining ratios remain locked in their previous scaling.

Formulate and analyze the role of a pressureless dark matter component in this framework. Specifically:

(a) Incorporate a cold dark matter fluid (with equation of state w = 0) into the modified Friedmann equations of the branch-cut model and determine how its energy density evolves through the contraction era, the bounce, and the subsequent expansion era.

(b) Determine whether the choice epsilon < 0 (associated with the reversed scaling behavior in the contraction phase) can be consistently identified with, or sourced by, the dark matter component; in particular, derive the relation between epsilon and the dark matter density parameter at the bounce.

(c) Establish whether dark matter is necessary for the existence of the bounce in this model, and whether structure-formation observables (e.g., the matter power spectrum on linear scales) are compatible with standard late-time cosmology in the resulting solution.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed explicitly as an open direction for future investigation in the branch-cut cosmology program, which is a recent and niche research line. No follow-up work appears to have definitively settled the role of dark matter in the branch-cut universe or its connection to a negative epsilon parameter.
